title: 5-Day_Machine_Gym_Workouts
author: Prabhu C.
desc: Transform your fitness routine with this 5-Day Machine Gym Workout Schedule, designed for those looking to build strength and muscle efficiently. Over the course of one week, you'll engage in targeted workouts that utilize gym machines to maximize your gains while minimizing the risk of injury. Each session focuses on different muscle groups, ensuring a balanced approach that promotes recovery and growth. Perfect for all fitness levels, this program will help you establish a solid foundation and elevate your training game. Get ready to crush your goals!

ex.note: Set handles at mid-chest. Feet planted; shoulder blades lightly back/down. Press forward and return slowly. · Wrists straight; elbows about 30–60° from torso; stop just before shoulder rolls forward. · Avoid: Elbows flared 90°; bouncing the stack; shrugging.
Seat so handles begin around upper chest. Press up/forward without lifting shoulders. · Chest stays tall; controlled 2–3 sec return. · Avoid: Too-high seat; hyperextending low back.

Set elbows/pads at chest height. Hug arms together in an arc; return only to a comfortable stretch. · Soft elbows; squeeze chest for 1 sec; shoulders remain down. · Avoid: Turning it into a shoulder stretch; slamming stack.

Elbows pinned by ribs. Extend forearms down; return until forearms are just above parallel. · Only elbows move; exhale as arms straighten. · Avoid: Leaning bodyweight into it; elbows drifting forward.
Seat firmly; elbows point forward/up as permitted by the machine. Extend without arching back. · Ribs down; neutral neck; full controlled extension. · Avoid: Flaring ribs; painful elbow range.
Set pad over upper chest. Curl ribs toward pelvis; do not pull with arms. · Small controlled spinal flexion; exhale at crunch. · Avoid: Pulling neck; using momentum.
Thigh pads secure. Start tall, pull elbows down toward side ribs, then control bar up. · Slight lean only; chest tall; shoulders do not shrug. · Avoid: Pulling behind neck; swinging torso.

Neutral spine. Pull handles toward lower ribs; allow shoulder blades to reach forward on return. · Elbows travel close to body; pause and squeeze shoulder blades. · Avoid: Rocking back; rounding low back.
Keep chest on pad; drive elbows back/down. · No low-back movement; slow stretch at front. · Avoid: Lifting chest off pad.
Chest on pad, arms near shoulder height. Open arms in a wide arc. · Lead with elbows; neck long; light load. · Avoid: Shrugging or overextending back.
Adjust pad under armpits. Curl smoothly; lower until arms nearly straight. · Keep upper arms on pad; squeeze without lifting shoulders. · Avoid: Locking elbows hard; using shoulder swing.
Choose a pace where you can speak in short sentences. · Steady breathing, relaxed grip, no all-out sprints. · Avoid: Holding rails; sudden intensity spikes.

Feet shoulder-width mid-platform. Lower sled until pelvis stays neutral, then push through whole foot. · Knees track over toes; low back stays on pad. · Avoid: Locking knees; hips curling under at depth.
Align knee joint with machine pivot. Extend to near-straight then lower slowly. · Seat tight; squeeze quads 1 sec at top. · Avoid: Kicking fast; locking knees aggressively.
Align knees with pivot; pad above ankles. Curl heels down/back, then control return. · Hips stay seated; no lumbar arch. · Avoid: Lifting hips off seat.
Pad above Achilles; curl heels toward glutes. · Keep hips pressed to pad. · Avoid: Arching low back; short reps.
Sit tall, bring pads together slowly and return under control. · Pelvis still; comfortable range. · Avoid: Forcing excessive stretch.
Stand sideways to cable, press handle away and resist rotation. · Ribs stacked over pelvis; exhale on press. · Avoid: Twisting torso toward the machine.
Seat so handles begin near ear level; back supported. Press upward slightly forward. · Forearms vertical; ribs down; finish without shrugging. · Avoid: Deep painful range; low-back arch.
Set pads just above elbows. Raise to shoulder height, then lower slowly. · Lead with elbows; wrists neutral; light load. · Avoid: Shrugging; swinging; going too heavy.
Same technique as Day 2; use a slightly different grip if comfortable. · Chest stays on pad; slow return. · Avoid: Neck tension.
Curl smoothly with upper arms fixed. · No shoulder lift; squeeze top. · Avoid: Bouncing bottom.
Use assistance/load that permits full control. Keep torso upright for triceps emphasis. · Elbows track back; shoulders down. · Avoid: Dropping into deep shoulder stretch.
Warm up first; brisk means challenging but controlled. · Return to easy pace immediately if form or breathing worsens. · Avoid: All-out sprinting; gripping handles tightly.
Pad sits in hip crease. Drive hips forward from heels; pause at full hip extension. · Ribs down; chin tucked; pelvis neutral at top. · Avoid: Hyperextending spine instead of hips.
Sit tall, open knees out; return slowly. Lean slightly forward only if machine feels better. · No bouncing; hold 1 sec open. · Avoid: Using momentum or forcing hip range.
Use full safe ankle range: lower heel slowly, rise onto big toe, pause. · Knee straight for standing; bent for seated. · Avoid: Bouncing; rolling ankle outward.
Hinge at hips with neutral spine, then stand tall. · Movement comes from hips; stop at body-straight. · Avoid: Overarching at top; rounding under load.
Same Day 3 setup; use deliberate tempo. · Control both directions. · Avoid: Rushing.
Move slowly; then 4 slow breaths and light chest/lat/hip-flexor stretches. · Exhale with effort; stretches should be mild, not painful. · Avoid: Holding breath; aggressive stretching.
